start.content: They still call me "the Leper," even now. It reminds everyone at my table what was done for me. When the Master first came to my door, they crossed the street to avoid me.

healed_by_jesus.content:
# UNLOCK_EVIDENCE: alabaster_jar
Healed -- yes. Leprosy took my skin, my fingernails, the flesh of my arms and legs. The physicians tried their poultices. Nothing worked. Then He touched me and said, "Be clean." And I was clean.

divine_touch.content: The touch was divine. The Master looked at my rotting flesh and saw something worth restoring. The villagers said it was unclean to be near me. He said it was unclean to stay away.

why_risk.content: Why risk ceremonial uncleanness? The Law required separation. Yet He crossed the street to reach me, and the Law yielded. I have thought about this often -- what divine authority allows Him to override the purity code?

authority_greater.content: The authority was greater than the Law itself. He did not need to consult the priests, did not need to purify afterward, did not need to make offerings for His own cleansing. He simply touched and it was done. If He had power over disease, what else could He do?

dinner_arranged.content:
The dinner was arranged because gratitude demanded it. How do you feed a man who gave you back your life? I offered my table -- and my forgiveness. Let my home be known for what happened that evening.
# UNLOCK_EVIDENCE: alabaster_jar

preparations.content: The preparations took all day. The finest lambs from my flock, the best wine from my cellar, bread baked fresh with honey. My servants set the table with my best linen. I wanted everything proper -- this was the Master's table.

guests_arrived.content: The guests arrived -- disciples, Pharisees, local townspeople. Lazarus was there, walking, talking, eating -- a walking miracle of the Master's power. My own sister Martha bustled about, ensuring everything was proper.

lazarus_present.content: Lazarus's presence -- the man who had been dead four days, now alive and eating fish from my table. The crowd whispered. The children pointed. The priests shifted uncomfortably. No one spoke of how he had been buried, how the earth had been sealed.

mary_act.content:
# UNLOCK_EVIDENCE: alabaster_jar
Then -- Mary moved. She opened a sealed alabaster jar and poured expensive nard on the Master's feet. The fragrance filled the entire house.

fragrance_intense.content: The fragrance was intense -- pure spikenard from the mountains of India, imported at great cost. The scent clung to every guest, filled every corner of the house. I could still smell it the next morning when I opened the door.

judas_objection.content: Judas objected loudly: "Why wasn't this sold for three hundred denarii and given to the poor?" He said it with the tone of compassion, but I knew him better. He kept the money bag, and the Master had noted that already.

judas_motive.content: His true motive was not compassion. The Gospel writer John saw it plainly -- Judas handled the money bag, and yes, he used to steal from it. His concern for the poor was a cover for his own greed. The Master knew.

masters_response.content: The Master's response was quiet but devastating: "Let her alone -- she has done a beautiful thing to me. The poor you will always have with you, but you will not always have me." He saw what no one else did -- this was preparation for His burial.

burial_prep.content: Preparation for burial. Mary understood what Judas could not -- the Master was not just entering Jerusalem as a king, but as a sacrifice. The anointing oil was the chrism, the fragrance the offering, the house the temple.

pattern_emerged.content: The pattern emerged clearly -- selection on Palm Sunday (triumphal entry), inspection in the Temple courts (the questioning), anointing at Bethany (Mary's act), and soon the sacrifice itself. The Passover lamb, just as the Exodus records it.

closing.content: I have very little left to give that would embarrass me to give. Let my house be remembered for what happened at my table, not for what I once was. Please -- eat. There is more than enough.
